other.content:
A photo of the verso shows an inscription on the stretcher bar. 
 
From Corcoran curatorial memo of 23 July 2007: 
“An inscription on the top stretcher bar in O'Keeffe's own hand reads "Emilia Oct - 48." 
Wondering whether this inscription might prompt us to reconsider the date of the painting, I contacted Barbara Lynes, author of the O'Keeffe catalogue raisonne. According to Lynes,"Emilia was a person who worked for O'Keeffe and probably helped her stretch canvases at various points in time." Lynes "suspect[s] that the stretcher was prepared then [1948]," but that "she returned to it in 1953, when she painted the picture."” 
 
Email from Barbara Lynes of 23 July 2008 confirms the inscription is in O’Keeffe’s hand (and that she had missed it when examining the painting for the CR). 
(Source: NGA, 2025)

cr_data.provenance:
(Doris Bry [1920-2014], New York).[1] (Noah Goldowsky Gallery, New York). Woodward Foundation, Washington, by 1966;[2] gift 1977 to the Corcoran Gallery of Art, Washington; acquired 2015 by the National Gallery of Art. (Source: NGA, 2025) 
 
[1] The first two owners are given in Barbara Buhler Lynes, _Georgie O'Keeffe: Catalogue Raisonné_, 2 vols., New Haven and London, 1999: 2:789, no. 1265. In a letter of 8 August 1953, the artist wrote to Edith Halpert that one of the four paintings she had sent that day to the Downtown Gallery was "Wall with Green Door/53" (Downtown Gallery Records, Archives of American Art, Smithsonian Institution, Washington, cited in Lynes 1999). The painting was lent by Miss O'Keeffe through the Downtown Gallery to a 1960 exhibition of her work at the Worcester Art Museum, and there is a Downtown Gallery label on the reverse, on which the painting is given number 166. 
 
[2] The 1966 date is according to Lynes 1999, 2:789, no. 1265.
remarks_1999: Abiquiú Notebooks, Whitney Archive in 1969 date 1952. Downtown Gallery Archive dates 1953. "Today I have sent you four painting by express. Wall with Green Door /53. ." (O'Keeffe to Edith Halpert, 8 August 1953, Archive of American Art). (Source: Lynes, 1999)
